groups.canonical_citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (Dept. of Neighborhood Development, Feb. 2017)
groups.conflict_note: This is a city agency policy (not a generally applicable ordinance) that binds only housing providers receiving DND funding/land or with BPDA inclusionary units; it does not cover ordinary market-rate multifamily landlords and may be preempted/limited by state and federal fair housing law where it conflicts.
groups.interaction: Applies only to a subset of city-funded/income-restricted housing; does not alter general state criminal-history screening rules (there is no comparable statewide statute).

groups.canonical_citation: Boston Fair Housing Regulations - Source of Income Protection
groups.interaction: Operates concurrently with the state source-of-income/public-assistance discrimination prohibition under M.G.L. c.151B, §4(10); both apply to Boston landlords.

groups.conflict_note: Bill was not enacted; final action was accompanied by a study order (see H.5035, 9/9/2024), effectively shelving it for the session.
groups.interaction: Would have authorized Boston to adopt local rent stabilization notwithstanding the statewide rent-control ban in M.G.L. c.40P, but never took effect.

groups.canonical_citation: Boston Municipal Code § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
groups.interaction: Supplements the state notice-to-quit requirements of M.G.L. c.186, §11 by adding a city-specific tenant-rights notice and reporting obligation; does not shorten or replace state notice periods.

groups.conflict_note: Sources disagree on status: one record treats the bill as merely 'pending,' but the official legislative history shows it was accompanied by a study order on 9/9/2024, indicating the bill was effectively shelved/failed rather than advancing.
groups.interaction: Would have authorized Boston to enact local just-cause eviction protections, but the measure never became law.

groups.canonical_citation: Cambridge Municipal Code ch. 14.04 (Fair Housing Ordinance)
groups.interaction: Operates concurrently with the state source-of-income/public-assistance discrimination prohibition under M.G.L. c.151B, §4(10).

groups.canonical_citation: Cambridge City Council Policy Order (2026) re: algorithmic rent-setting software ban
groups.conflict_note: This is only a policy order directing staff to draft a future ordinance; no ordinance text, scope, or effective date yet exists, and it may eventually be superseded or preempted by a statewide law if one of the pending state bills (H.5222/S.2983) is enacted first.
groups.interaction: If Cambridge eventually enacts an ordinance, it would operate alongside any statewide algorithmic rent-setting ban enacted via H.5222 or S.2983; currently neither level has a binding rule in force.

groups.interaction: Would apply statewide, including in cities like Cambridge considering local algorithmic rent-setting bans; not yet in force.

groups.canonical_citation: Mass. Initiative Petition 25-21 (2026); see Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893
groups.conflict_note: The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court ruled the petition unconstitutional (religious-facility exemption violated Article 48) and blocked it from the November 2026 ballot; it never took effect and does not alter the existing statewide ban on local rent control under M.G.L. c.40P.
groups.interaction: Would have repealed/superseded the statewide rent-control ban in M.G.L. c.40P had it passed and taken effect; it did not become law.

Sets the baseline 14-day notice-to-quit requirement for nonpayment statewide; Boston's Housing Stability Notification Act adds an additional tenant-rights notice on top of this state requirement.

groups.interaction: Distinct from the broker-fee statute (M.G.L. c.112, §87DDD 1/2); together they govern what tenants may be charged before and during move-in.
